1

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V.
Act, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- on account of the death of Sri. Venkataramanna in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, are as follows:
On 26.10.2023 at about 12.30 p.m., the deceased was going towards his village G u d i p a l l i f r o m N . V a d d a h a l l i b y r i d i n g a T V S X L m o p e d b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-07-ED-0019 and when he reached near Yaluvalli Cross, on Mulabagal-Punganur road, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, the driver of KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and came from opposite direction i.e., from Punganur side and dashed violently against the motor cycle in which the deceased was proceeding.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries on the spot.
Thereafter, the deceased dead body was shifted to Government Hospital, Mulabagal, wherein, PM examination was conducted.
The deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 50 years at the time of accident.
He was a mason mesthri working under different employers and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month and in near future he would have earned more than Rs.50,000/- per month if he was alive.
He was the only bread earner of the family and petitioners were entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners are put to lot of mental agony and untold misery and lost their bread earner.
The respondent is the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notice, respondent appeared and filed written statement by contending that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased as he was driving his two-wheeler TVS Excel bearing No.KA-07-ED-0019 in rash and negligent manner and tried to avoid pat hole in his side and lost control over his two-wheeler without following the rules in the middle of the road and fell down on the tar road and sustained head injury.

The incident occurred by the deceased own negligence and self fall and not by the driver of the bus and bus was not even touch the two- wheeler and there was no negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:

sentences.text: Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives and dependents of deceased Sri. Venkataramanna?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Sri. Venkataramanna had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 26.10.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. near Yaluvahalli Cross, on Mulabagal-Punganur road, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar district, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-07-F-1675 as alleged?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?

If so, what amount and from whom?
4.
What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the first petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.

The respondent examined the driver of the bus as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 to 4.
6.
Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the material evidence that is available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per final orders  for the following.-
 REASONS ISSUE NO.2:
8.

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced certified copies of FIR,
complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, inquest report, PM report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
As per the documents, Ex.P1- FIR came to be registered on the basis of first information given by one Nagesh, who is son of the deceased.
In the first information the informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675.
The said information is lodged on 26.10.2023 by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus and alleged accident at 12.30 to 1.00 p.m. of the same day.
Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar along with Ex.P3 rough sketch of the alleged accident spot.

If we consider the contents of spot mahazar, the accident spot is very near to the left side edge of the Ramadevi vs Ksrtc on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45188397/
3 road.
This establishes that the driver of the KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675 came to wrong side in a turning that too to his extreme right side and caused the accident.
As per the Ex.P3 rough sketch and mahazar the accident spot is in the western edge of the road ie., left side edge of the road in which the deceased was proceeding.

10. The respondent has taken specific contention that the offending bus has not touched the motor cycle of the deceased whereas the deceased himself while avoiding the pathole got fell down on the road and the bus is no where involved in the accident.

Ex.P4 is IMV report wherein on the KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675, no fresh damages found but, motorcycle of the deceased has got damages in its handle, crash guard and front brake lever.
To establish its defence the respondent examined its driver as RW.1 and produced Ex.R1 to R3 documents.

If we perused the Ex.R1 in the said Ex.R1, the RW.1 himself stated that the handle of the motor cycle of the deceased dashed against the front right side head light (      
-07--0019            ,          
            
       .)
As per this content of Ex.R1 the handle of the motor cycle dashed against the right side front corner of the bus.

It is very important to note that the content of Ex.R1 is totally against the pleadings of written statement whereas in the written statement the defendant taken a contention that the bus never touched the said motor cycle of the deceased.
11. No evidence is available to hold the existence of pot holes as contended by the respondent in the written statement.
In the mahazar as per Ex.P3 and rough sketch as per Ex.P4 also the IO has not found any pot holes in the accident spot.
It is very important to note that the conductor of the bus is not examined by the respondent and no reasons are assigned by the respondent for not examining its conductor.

12. By considering the Ex.P2 mahazar Ex.P3- rough sketch it is found that the accident has happened due to the negligence of the driver of KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No.
KA-07-F-1675 wherein the driver of KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675 was rash and negligent in his driving and dashed against the deceased motorcycle by coming to his extreme right side/wrong side.
13. Ex.P6 is post mortem report and Ex.P6 is inquest.
Both these documents are mentioned with injuries sustained by the deceased.
By considering the same and the nature of the injuries shows that the deceased died due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

14. Upon receiving the complaint, police have registered FIR against the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675 The police after completion of investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 & 304(A) of IPC and Ramadevi vs Ksrtc on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45188397/
4 Sec.134(a)(b) of the IMV Act.
In the charge sheet also the IO has opined that the accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675

The head of the charge sheet is marked at Ex.P7 Even though the driver of KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675 examined himself as R.W1 failed to rebut the evidence adduced by the petitioner and also not produced any independent evidence to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence the contents of documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7 wherein in the investigation the investigation officer has found the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-07-F-1675 cannot be brush aside.

15. Even though the PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent nothing has been elicited to hold that the accident is caused due to the negligence of the deceased and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No. KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No.
KA-07-F-1675 16.
As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioner there are sufficient materials to show that, deceased died in the accident dated 26.10.2023 which is caused by the driver of the KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F- 1675.
Accordingly issue No.2 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.1 17.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that the deceased Venkataramanna on 26.10.2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by driver of KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675.
18.
As contended in the petition that the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased.
The respondent do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioner with deceased.

The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of petitioners and deceased which are marked under Ex.P.8 and notarized copy of Ration card of petitioners is marked under Ex.P.9.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhaar cards and ration card are compared with the original documents and found correct.
19. As per these documents the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the minor son of the deceased, but the respondent do not dispute the relationship of the petitioners with deceased.
The respondent do not dispute the Aadhaar cards and Ration card produced by the petitioners.
The respondent has not adduced any contrary evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

20. In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioners is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased and they are dependents of the deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, issue No.1 Ramadevi vs Ksrtc on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45188397/
5 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE No.3 21.

As held herein above, the petitioners proved that the deceased Venkataramanna died on 26.10.2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of the KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675.
22.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
As per Ex.P.11 -Aadhaar card of the deceased Venkataramanna was born on 01.01.1973
, the accident took place in the year-2023,
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 50 years.
In the Ex.P6- PM report the age of the deceased is shown as 52 years.

The learned counsel for the petitioner placed his reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka by arguing that the completed years of the deceased has to be considered to compute the age of the deceased.

In the case of Divisional Constroller, MSRTC Vs. Bismilla and others in MFA No.101337 and 101664 /2021 dated 19-06-2023 reported in 2024 ACJ 173 wherein it held as follows;
"16.

entities.text: Divisional Constroller, MSRTC Vs. Bismilla and others in MFA No.101337 and 101664 /2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of the Corporation that the Tribunal has committed error 13 in applying multiplier as the deceased was aged 50 years 6 months.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarala Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation 26 Limited and another5 has determined the multiplier based on the age group of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarala Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation 26 Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the multiplier is 13 for the age group between 46-50 and 11 multiplier for age group between 51-55.
Keeping in mind the ratio laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarala Varma referred supra

,
we are of the considered view that the deceased was in age group of 46-50 and not 51-55 as he has not completed 51 years of age on the date of accident.

Hence, we are of the view that the Tribunal has justified in applying the multiplier of 13 which does not call for interference''.
23.
In the present case also as per the Ex.P8 Aadhar card of the deceased the date of birth of the deceased was 01-01-1973 and the date of accident is 26-10-2023.
As such as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 50 years 9 months 9 days.
Thereby the deceased has completed the age of 50 years and falls under the age group of 46 to 50.
Hence by relying on the said precedent the age of the deceased is considered as 50 years.

24. As stated in the petition deceased was working as construction labour and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

In the absence of documents, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,000/- as the accident is of the year 2023 and the annual income comes to Rs.1,92,000/-.
25.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 13.

Since the deceased left his wife and son, it is considered that, there are two dependents of deceased, hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Ramadevi vs Ksrtc on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45188397/
6 Rs.16,64,000/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 13= Rs.24,96,000/- minus 1/3rd = Rs.8,32,000/-).

26. In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

Once notional income is determined,
the effects of inflation would equally apply.
Further, no one would ever say that the improvements in skills that come with experience do not take place in the domain of work within the household.

It is worth nothing that, although not extensively discussed, this Court has been granting future prospects even in cases pertaining to notional income, as has been highlighted by my learned brother, Surya Kant, J., in his opinion (Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654:
Sunita Tokas V. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2019) 20 SCC 688)".
28.

entities.text: Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sunita Tokas V. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2019) 20 SCC 688)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the above decisions 25% out of loss of dependency has to be granted towards future prospects which would Rs.4,16,000/-.
29.
The Petitioners No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of deceased.
The petitioner No.1 lost her loving and caring husband and petitioner no.2 lost his caring and loving father.
Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- ( Rs.44,000/-. Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.

Further I inclined to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of lover and affection and Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
As per Ex.R3 the interim compensation of Rs.25,000/- is paid by respondent.
The Ex.R3 is not disputed by the petitioners.
Thereby the said amount of interim compensation of Rs.25,000/- shall be deducted in the total amount of compensation.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 16,64,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 4,16,000/-

 compensation 30. Liability:-
The respondent is the owner and insurer of the KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675 hence, it is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
31. It is argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that the interest cannot be awarded on the future prospectus as it is awarded for future income in lump sum.

In this regard the learned counsel for petitioner by praying to award the interest for the future prospectus also relied on the following judgment:
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case of Reliance General Ins. Co. Ltd.,
Vs. Supreeth S and others in MFA No.511/2020 dated 01-08-2024 reported in 2024 ACJ 2257 wherein it is held as follows;
"33.
Despite of the aforementioned facts, in this case, the insurance company has raised a plea that it is not liable to pay any interest on the amount awarded towards loss of future prospects.

The justification in such a plea can be verified through the following illustration:
"'X' met with an accident and succumbed to injuries in the year 2014.
'Y' his wife, A and B, their children, files a petition claiming compensation in the light of the death of their bread winner.
The insurance company enters into appearance.

On contest,
the Tribunal allows the claim petition in the year 2018 and awards a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- as compensation.
The insurance company prefers appeal and the appeal gets dismissed in the year 2022 upholding the award of the Tribunal.
The insurance company approaches the Hon'ble Apex Court and the Hon'ble Apex Court passes judgment in the year 2024 negating the pleas taken by the insurance company.
Thus, the award attains finality in the year 2024.
'Y' the wife, A and B the children of the deceased 'X' would be bearing legal expenses for the entire period of ten years i.e. from 2014 to 2024.

That apart, 'Y' would be at liability to provide Ramadevi vs Ksrtc on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45188397/
8 education to her children either by begging or by borrowing.
For all the three to survive, food, shelter and clothing are required.
Therefore, 'Y' might have incurred debts, would have sold out any valuable property, or would have mortgaged the said property or might have pledged the valuable articles like gold.
Thus, for all the expenditure incurred for the ten years, 'Y' and her children A and B would be liable to pay interest.
On the other hand, the insurance company would be reaping the profit in the form of interest on the amount that fell due to the claimants for all the said ten years period."

34. In the circumstances aforementioned which would be present in almost all motor vehicles claims, if the dependents are denied with the interest over the amount awarded under the head 'loss of future prospects', it would be most unjustifiable.
The reasons are two fold.
(i) Despite making stringent provisions for settlement of claims at the earliest date, it is taking years and decades for settlement of claims.
In the interregnum period, the survival of claimants would be based on the available resources and the capability of getting debts.

(ii) The insurance companies who are liable to pay the compensation as soon as possible as indicated under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 would be enjoying the principle amount and the fruits that accrued through the investment of the principle amount.
35. The amount payable to the claimants which lies with the insurance companies for years together is one way the debt the insurance companies have to make good to the claimants.

When the insurance companies are enjoying the fruits of the said amount and the accrued interest for years together, they cannot take plea that they are not liable to pay interest to the claimants over the amount which they are liable.
36. In the case on hand, the accident occurred in the year 2014 and the claim is not settled till this day.
Thus, the amount which the claimants are legally entitled to is being enjoyed by the insurance company for a long period of ten years.
Now the insurance company has taken a plea that it is not liable to pay the interest on future prospects.

37. The plea taken by the insurance company that it is not liable to pay interest on the future prospects, as the amount awarded under that head would be the future earnings of the deceased is not justifiable due to the reason that the claimants are not being paid the entire earnings of the deceased which he would have earned had he been alive.
Cases where there is no proof in certainty regarding exact income, the Courts are taking notional income into consideration.

Either applying appropriate multiplier as per the decision in Sarala Verma's case or taking percentage of the said income towards future prospects as per the decision in Pranay Sethi's case is on probabilities but not on exact figures.
In no case, the claimants get the exact amount which the deceased would have earned had he been alive.
In all cases the amount which the claimants would get for their livelihood through the deceased would be many times more than the actual amount awarded.
That apart, the insurance companies are depositing the compensation years after the date of accident which is in clear violation of Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Ramadevi vs Ksrtc on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45188397/
9 38.
Further more, award of amount as compensation is a one time procedure.

Even if in the future course it is found that the deceased would have earned much more amount in the light of hike in his position and global opportunities, the Tribunals will not order payment of any further amount and insurance companies will not be made liable on that count.

Such being the case, this Court is of the view that the insurance companies are liable to pay the awarded amount including the amount awarded under the head future prospects together with banking rate of interest which is prevalent during relevant time.
Thus, we ultimately hold that, the insurance company cannot escape from the liability to pay interest on the future prospects''.
Thereby in the above quoted judgment the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has clearly held that the amount awarded under the head of future prospectus also carries the rate of interest.

Hence the respondent corporation is liable to pay the compensation along with the interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
32.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.21,82,000/-
(Rupees Twenty one lakhs eighty two thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 60:40.

Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% shall be released in favour petitioner No.1 on her proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in her name.
The entire amount awarded to petitioner No.2 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in his name in any Scheduled Bank, till he attain the age of majority.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 11th day of April, 2025).

In the charge sheet also the IO has opined that the accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1675
In the absence of rebuttal evidence the contents of documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7 wherein in the investigation the investigation officer has found the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg.
15. Even though the PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent nothing has been elicited to hold that the accident is caused due to the negligence of the deceased and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No. KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No.
KA-07-F-1675 16.
As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioner there are sufficient materials to show that, deceased died in the accident dated 26.10.2023 which is caused by the driver of the KSRTC Rajahamsa bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F- 1675.
The respondent has not adduced any contrary evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 50 years.
,
we are of the considered view that the deceased was in age group of 46-50 and not 51-55 as he has not completed 51 years of age on the date of accident.
(i) Despite making stringent provisions for settlement of claims at the earliest date, it is taking years and decades for settlement of claims.
In the interregnum period, the survival of claimants would be based on the available resources and the capability of getting debts.
(ii) The insurance companies who are liable to pay the compensation as soon as possible as indicated under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 would be enjoying the principle amount and the fruits that accrued through the investment of the principle amount.
35. The amount payable to the claimants which lies with the insurance companies for years together is one way the debt the insurance companies have to make good to the claimants.
When the insurance companies are enjoying the fruits of the said amount and the accrued interest for years together, they cannot take plea that they are not liable to pay interest to the claimants over the amount which they are liable.
Thus, the amount which the claimants are legally entitled to is being enjoyed by the insurance company for a long period of ten years.
Now the insurance company has taken a plea that it is not liable to pay the interest on future prospects.
37. The plea taken by the insurance company that it is not liable to pay interest on the future prospects, as the amount awarded under that head would be the future earnings of the deceased is not justifiable due to the reason that the claimants are not being paid the entire earnings of the deceased which he would have earned had he been alive.
Cases where there is no proof in certainty regarding exact income, the Courts are taking notional income into consideration.
Either applying appropriate multiplier as per the decision in Sarala Verma's case or taking percentage of the said income towards future prospects as per the decision in Pranay Sethi's case is on probabilities but not on exact figures.
In no case, the claimants get the exact amount which the deceased would have earned had he been alive.
In all cases the amount which the claimants would get for their livelihood through the deceased would be many times more than the actual amount awarded.
That apart, the insurance companies are depositing the compensation years after the date of accident which is in clear violation of Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Further more, award of amount as compensation is a one time procedure.
Even if in the future course it is found that the deceased would have earned much more amount in the light of hike in his position and global opportunities, the Tribunals will not order payment of any further amount and insurance companies will not be made liable on that count.
